worked_solution:
Let's simplify one of the given integrals:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{7}^{2}(-5)\,f(x)\,\text{d}x & =15 \\ (-5){\int }_{7}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x & =15 \\ 5{\int }_{2}^{7}f(x)\,\text{d}x & =15 \\ {\int }_{2}^{7}f(x)\,\text{d}x & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Then, from the adjacent intervals rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1}^{7}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{-1}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{2}^{7}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =1+3 \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$
